analysis: The only changed file in this batch is landing/package-lock.json, the marketing/landing site's npm lockfile. The visible change bumps the direct dependency next from 16.2.6 to 16.4.1 (head line 11) and moves the optional sharp image stack from 0.34.5 to 0.35.5. Related libvips packages move from 1.2.4 to 1.3.4 (for example head lines 586-651). Several sharp platform packages are added, such as @img/sharp-freebsd-wasm32 at head line 629. Node engine constraints are loosened to >=20.9.0. The resolved URLs point at registry.npmjs.org and carry sha512 integrity values, so no non-registry source, git dependency or integrity removal is visible. The new libvips packages carry LGPL-3.0-or-later licenses, which is a licensing concern, not a security one. This is web-frontend dependency maintenance. It does not touch the provider process, coordinator WebSocket contract (TB-002), operator boundary (TB-003), inference engine (TB-007), attestation (TB-009/TB-011), the fan helper (TB-010) or the add-on hold socket (TB-012). It does not touch any asset (A-001 to A-018), and none of the cited threat definitions (T-009, T-033, T-034) applies. The patch excerpt and range map for the lockfile are partly truncated. I could not verify the full set of changed lines, such as the lines 1600-1663 block on the head side, or whether the new next 16.4.1 entry in node_modules matches the root declaration, because that region is outside the supplied units. The next entry that the lock declares at root (16.4.1) is not visible in the supplied head text, so a lock/package.json consistency check cannot be made here. The remaining integration question is whether landing/package.json was updated consistently and whether the sharp 0.35.x install scripts (hasInstallScript) behave as expected. I identified no security regression in the examined lines.
